own_scenes.desc: Kris Parker se crió junto al 1520 de Sedgwick Avenue y vivió de adolescente en el albergue del Franklin Avenue Armory, donde conoció al trabajador social Scott Sterling: KRS-One y DJ Scott La Rock. Mr. Magic despreció su maqueta en Power Play («eso no es hip hop de verdad») y, convencidos de que «The Bridge» decía que el hip hop había nacido en Queens, respondieron con «South Bronx», que DJ Red Alert y Paradise Gray (nueve veces en una noche en el Latin Quarter) convirtieron en éxito. Tras «Kill That Noise» de Shan llegó el golpe definitivo, «The Bridge Is Over», sobre ritmo de reggae, con los sonidos de la cinta de baterías que Marley se dejó en el estudio y Ced-Gee se quedó. Fue la primera gran rivalidad del rap, de puro deporte, sin violencia. Criminal Minded (B-Boy, 1987) los mostraba con armas; meses después Scott La Rock murió de un disparo al mediar en una pelea en Highbridge Gardens. Jive mantuvo el contrato: KRS-One se volvió el gran guardián de la cultura, conferenciante en universidades.

Marley Marl y la Juice Crew

refs.q: That record played like nine times in one night, and the crowd went bananas every fucking time.
refs.para: So, when the club opened, I played it again and the early crowd blew up. And so when my house DJs came, they played it four or five times before Red Alert even came to the club. So by the time Red got there, that shit was busting crazy. The crowd blew up. And the rest was history. Red played it four more times that night. That record played like nine times in one night, and the crowd went bananas every fucking time. From the first time it ever spun, we knew it was a mega-hit.

So now, with him telling me that, I’m going back through Ced-Gee’s productions and I’m noticing my kicks and my snares on his shit. I’m hearing Ultramagnetic records, some of them, some BDP joints with my drum sounds on it and shit. That was the golden reel.
MC Shan (Juice Crew, Queensbridge): That’s what we did back then. That was the whole entertainment portion of what we did. It wasn’t always about preaching a message. We did this for sport.
